entries.name: Monitor
entries.description:
Start a background monitor that streams events from a long-running script. Each stdout line is an event — you keep working and notifications arrive in the chat. Events arrive on their own schedule and are not replies from the user, even if one lands while you're waiting for the user to answer a question.

Pick by how many notifications you need:
- **One** ("tell me when the server is ready / the build finishes") → use **Bash with `run_in_background`** and a command that exits when the condition is true, e.g. `until grep -q "Ready in" dev.log; do sleep 0.5; done`. You get a single completion notification when it exits.
- **One per occurrence, until the monitor expires (re-arm to continue)** ("tell me every time an ERROR line appears") → Monitor with an unbounded command (`tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, `while true`).
- **One per occurrence, until a known end** ("emit each CI step result, stop when the run completes") → Monitor with a command that emits lines and then exits.

Your script's stdout is the event stream. Each line becomes a notification. Exit ends the watch.

  # Each matching log line is an event
  tail -f /var/log/app.log | grep --line-buffered "ERROR"

  # Each file change is an event
  inotifywait -m --format '%e %f' /watched/dir

  # Poll GitHub for new PR comments and emit one line per new comment
  last=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
  while true; do
    now=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
    gh api "repos/owner/repo/issues/123/comments?since=$last" --jq '.[] | "\(.user.login): \(.body)"'
    last=$now; sleep 30
  done

  # Node script that emits events as they arrive (e.g. WebSocket listener)
  node watch-for-events.js

  # Per-occurrence with a natural end: emit each CI check as it lands, exit when the run completes
  prev=""
  while true; do
    s=$(gh pr checks 123 --json name,bucket)
    cur=$(jq -r '.[] | select(.bucket!="pending") | "\(.name): \(.bucket)"' <<<"$s" | sort)
    comm -13 <(echo "$prev") <(echo "$cur")
    prev=$cur
    jq -e 'all(.bucket!="pending")' <<<"$s" >/dev/null && break
    sleep 30
  done

**Don't use an unbounded command for a single notification.** `tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, and `while true` never exit on their own, so the monitor stays armed until timeout even after the event has fired. For "tell me when X is ready," use Bash `run_in_background` with an `until` loop instead (one notification, ends in seconds). Note that `tail -f log | grep -m 1 ...` does *not* fix this: if the log goes quiet after the match, `tail` never receives SIGPIPE and the pipeline hangs anyway.

**Script quality:**
- Every pipe stage must flush per line or matches sit in its buffer unseen: `grep` needs `--line-buffered`, `awk` needs `fflush()`. `head` cannot flush at all — `| head -N` delivers nothing until N matches accumulate, then ends the stream.
- In poll loops, handle transient failures (`curl ... || true`) — one failed request shouldn't kill the monitor.
- Poll intervals: 30s+ for remote APIs (rate limits), 0.5-1s for local checks.
- Write a specific `description` — it appears in every notification ("errors in deploy.log" not "watching logs").
- Only stdout is the event stream. Stderr goes to the output file (readable via Read) but does not trigger notifications — for a command you run directly (e.g. `python train.py 2>&1 | grep --line-buffered ...`), merge stderr with `2>&1` so its failures reach your filter. (No effect on `tail -f` of an existing log — that file only contains what its writer redirected.)

**Coverage — silence is not success.** When watching a job or process for an outcome, your filter must match every terminal state, not just the happy path. A monitor that greps only for the success marker stays silent through a crashloop, a hung process, or an unexpected exit — and silence looks identical to "still running." Before arming, ask: *if this process crashed right now, would my filter emit anything?* If not, widen it.

  # Wrong — silent on crash, hang, or any non-success exit
  tail -f run.log | grep --line-buffered "elapsed_steps="

  # Right — one alternation covering progress + the failure signatures you'd act on
  tail -f run.log | grep -E --line-buffered "elapsed_steps=|Traceback|Error|FAILED|assert|Killed|OOM"

For poll loops checking job state, emit on every terminal status (`succeeded|failed|cancelled|timeout`), not just success. If you cannot confidently enumerate the failure signatures, broaden the grep alternation rather than narrow it — some extra noise is better than missing a crashloop.

**Output volume**: Every stdout line is a conversation message, so the filter should be selective — but selective means "the lines you'd act on," not "only good news." Never pipe raw logs; filter to exactly the success and failure signals you care about. Monitors that produce too many events are automatically stopped; restart with a tighter filter if this happens.

Stdout lines within 200ms are batched into a single notification, so multiline output from a single event groups naturally.

The script runs in the same shell environment as Bash. Exit ends the watch (exit code is reported). Every monitor expires after `timeout_ms` (default 5 minutes, at most 30 minutes): it is killed and you get one notice with the event count. Re-arm it if you still need the watch; for a long watch (PR monitoring, log tails) set `timeout_ms` to the maximum and re-arm on each expiry, and widen the filter if an expiry with no events was unexpected. Use TaskStop to cancel early.
**ws source** — open a WebSocket and stream each incoming text frame as an event. No shell, no polling: the server pushes, you get notified.

  Monitor({
    ws: {url: 'wss://events.example.com/stream', protocols: ['v1']},
    description: 'deploy events',
  })

Each text frame becomes one notification (multiline frames stay as one event). Binary frames are reported as `[binary frame, N bytes]` rather than passed through. Socket close ends the watch with the close code surfaced; errors are surfaced before close. Same rate limiting as bash — a firehose will be suppressed and eventually stopped, so subscribe to a filtered feed where one exists.

Prefer this over `command: 'websocat wss://…'` — it avoids the extra process and line-buffering pitfalls. Use bash when you need to transform or filter frames with shell tools before they become events.

When an event lands that the user would want to act on now — an error appeared, the status they were waiting on flipped — send a PushNotification. Not every event is worth a push; the ones that change what they'd do next are.

description.description: Short human-readable description of what you are monitoring (shown in notifications).

timeout_ms.description: Kill the monitor after this deadline. Default 300000ms. Deadlines above 1800000ms are capped to 1800000ms. You are notified at expiry and can re-arm.

command.description: Shell command or script. Each stdout line is an event; exit ends the watch.

ws.description: WebSocket to open. Each text frame is an event; binary frames are reported as a placeholder line. Socket close ends the watch. Cannot be combined with command.

content.content:
**The computation-only exemption.** `slice_start`, `plan_set` and `activity_cancel` run without a card. `slice_start` replaces a computed result and refuses to take over a run it did not start unless `preempt`, which brings the card back. `plan_set` records the agent's own statement, shown in the plan card, and changes nothing in the project. `activity_cancel` stops only what the tools started: a waiting proposal, a job the tools queued, or the slice `slice_start` started while that run lasts; once that run has ended, a slice the person starts is not stopped by the old handle (coordinator test). The person can start any of these again.

**Not tripped here.** No camera frames (`printer_camera_snapshot` is not built), no print upload (`print_send` is not built), no binding beyond loopback, no grants that outlive a restart.

## Verification commands and limits of current evidence

From the repository root on the existing macOS development build:

```sh
cmake --build build/arm64 --config RelWithDebInfo --target OrcaSlicer agent_bridge_tests shell_integration_harness -- -j6
build/arm64/tests/agent/RelWithDebInfo/agent_bridge_tests.app/Contents/MacOS/agent_bridge_tests --order rand --warn NoAssertions
python3 -m unittest discover -s tests/mcp -v
npm --prefix src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI test
build/arm64/tests/shell/RelWithDebInfo/JusPrinShellHarness.app/Contents/MacOS/JusPrinShellHarness --mcp-bridge
```

The same run on the Windows verification machine, where the generator is Visual Studio and there is no `python3`:

```sh
cmake --build build --config Release --target OrcaSlicer agent_bridge_tests shell_integration_harness -- -m
build/tests/agent/Release/agent_bridge_tests.exe --order rand --warn NoAssertions
npm --prefix src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI test
build/tests/shell/Release/shell_integration_harness.exe --mcp-bridge
```

The workspace adapter harness runs there too, and passes (617 checks, exit 0, as of 2026-09-17). Put the app's `src\Release` on `PATH`, or the exe cannot load the `api-ms-win-crt` DLLs, and read the exit code with `$LASTEXITCODE` in PowerShell:

```powershell
$env:PATH = "$PWD\build\src\Release;$env:PATH"
build\tests\workspace\Release\workspace_adapter_integration_harness.exe
```

On 2026-09-16 it failed on Windows: `select_object(0)` returned false after `load_files`, seven checks failed, and the process died with `0xC0000005`. The test code was not stale. The cause was the machine setup. The Mesa provisioning script put `opengl32.dll` only in `mesa\`, where only the app launcher looks for it. A harness has no launcher, so this one ran on the system's GL 1.1 and its canvas never initialized. Selection is built from the canvas's volumes, so nothing could be selected, and the gizmo check then opened a paint gizmo with nothing selected. The script now also copies `opengl32.dll` beside each harness (see "Software GL on Windows machines without a GPU" in [engineering-method.md](engineering-method.md)); re-run it on existing build trees. With GL in place, two harness faults surfaced that only Windows shows:

- The move-event check asserted that the move was the last change. On Windows, queued `EVT_GLCANVAS_OBJECT_SELECT` events publish two Selection-only changes after it, so the check now skips those.
- The data-directory cleanup threw, because the open log file cannot be deleted, and the uncaught exception turned a PASS into `0xC0000409`. It now warns instead, as the shell harness already did.

content.text:
It did get smaller. The app code is 156 lines shorter than before (1,239 added, 1,395 removed), and the tests come out even at 582 each way. The earlier diff summaries undercounted the deletions, because they listed files `git` was tracking as changed and left out the deleted spool files.

| | Added | Removed |
|---|---|---|
| App code | 1,239 | 1,395 |
| Tests | 582 | 582 |
| Docs | 2 | 2 |

**Removing spools on its own took out about 1,000 lines.** That's `SpoolStore` (361), `SpoolMenu` (533), the seeding and swap code in `StatusRow`, the store plumbing through Home, the printer panel, the setup chat and the `printer_change` tool, plus the 337-line spool store test.

**Most of what I added is turn 23's new features, not spool replacement:**
- dots for every slot, with fading, the "+n" fold and shrinking (`FilamentChipModel`, 99 lines, kept apart so it can be unit-tested; dot drawing in `HeaderControls`, about 50)
- the slot list, per-slot views and "Add a slot"
- the colour row with Orca's saved colours and the system picker
- the "Use what's loaded on the printer…" row, its offline state, and the hand-off to Orca's sync
- per-slot filament selection that follows Orca's colour rule, and re-picking after a nozzle change
- the colour dot on the chat note

`FilamentMenu` (391 lines plus a 102-line header) came out close to the size of the spool menu it replaced (533). It lost rename, recolour, remove and "new spool", and gained slots, colours and trays.

**Where it could be leaner:**
- The harness is up about 210 net lines, mostly new scenarios (a filament change through the menu, slots, fading, the tray row and sync, nozzle re-pick). It also has diagnostic prints I added while chasing the fade failure; those come out before I commit.
- The chip tooltip's slot-by-slot list and the custom colour-cell widget are the most optional pieces. I can cut them if you want the minimum.

The three harness reruns are still going; I'll report when they finish.

No `spools` (or an empty array) reports no AMS at all, same as before this
field existed. A non-empty array reports one AMS unit (id `"0"`) with one
tray per spool, up to 4:

```json
{"spools": [{"subBrands": "PLA Matte", "trayType": "PLA", "colour": "5F7D4FFF"}]}
```

`subBrands` is what `PrinterDiscovery.cpp` reads back as the spool's name
when set (ahead of `trayType`), so it is the field worth setting for a
saved/network-printer card or receipt to show something. `trayType` is the
spool's material (Home's Loaded row names it); the fake sends it with an
empty `tray_info_idx`, since upstream ignores a type that arrives without
one. `colour` is optional: a spool without it reports no colour, and Home
draws no swatch for it.

Delete the file, or set `"offline": false` and `"state":"idle"`, to return to Idle.

content.text:
Turn 23 is built on branch `claude/filament-chip` (from `jusprin-newui` at `b7f7fc4ee6`). The saved-spool concept is gone and the chip and filament menu now use only what OrcaSlicer stores. Nothing is committed yet. No OrcaSlicer-owned file changed: every edit is in the fork's `JusPrin` code, its tests, or its docs.

**What's in:**
- **Spools removed:** the spool store, its tests, the automatic seeding, and the spool menu's rename, recolour and remove. Home's "Loaded" row now shows only trays a connected printer reports. The setup chat's `printer_change` tool changes the nozzle only, and the chat context lists only reported trays.
- **Chip:** printer nickname and nozzle on the left; if the nozzles differ it shows each size ("0.4 / 0.6"). On the right, one dot per slot: faded if the current plate doesn't use it, unused slots folded into "+n" past 8, dots shrunk when more than 8 are in use. The label is the filament's short name when the used slots share one filament, otherwise "N filaments".
- **Filament menu:**
  - It stays open after a click, so a filament and a colour can change in one visit.
  - Colour row: the slot's colour and Orca's saved colours, plus "+" for the system picker.
  - Below that: installed filaments that fit, brand then name, then Other filament…, Filament settings… and Add a slot.
  - With several slots, a slot list opens first.
  - "Use what's loaded on the printer…" appears only when the printer reports trays, greyed with the reason when it's offline.
- **After a change:** one chat line per menu visit, led by a colour dot. A colour-only change adds no line.
- **Your four decisions:**
  - Orca's colour rule: a preset with a default colour brings it; otherwise the slot keeps its colour.
  - "Other filament…" opens Orca's own filament page.
  - Changing the nozzle runs Orca's compatibility pass.
  - Klipper lanes are left for the task chip I created.

**Results:**
- Page tests: Agent 204, Home 61, both type-check.
- Native suites: `jusprin_tests` 52 cases, `agent_bridge_tests` 258, `jusprin_fake_bambu_tests` 10.
- Shell harness in the real app:
  - `--printer-setup`: all 166 checks pass.
  - `--home-live` (fake Bambu with trays): all 70 checks pass.
  - Default run: 433 of 434 pass. The one failure, `print_opens_cancellable_native_preflight`, fails the same way in another session's run of this branch from before my changes.

**Two open questions from the handoff, now answered:**
- **Orca's sync works with the sidebar hidden.** With the fake printer's two trays, it copied Bambu PLA Matte in its colour and Bambu PETG HF into the project. When nothing needs a choice, Orca syncs without showing any dialog. This needed the fake printer to send a real filament id per tray, as hardware does; without one, Orca skipped every tray.
- **A nozzle change can now modify the project.** Going to 0.6 mm replaced "0.20mm Standard @BBL X1C" with "0.30mm Standard @BBL X1C 0.6 nozzle". That contradicts an earlier rule (commit `7f66e75b07`) that a nozzle change leaves the project untouched, so I changed that check. The project now counts as changed only when a preset had to be replaced.

**Where it differs from the design, or isn't checked yet:**
- Hover shows each slot as text only; a plain tooltip can't draw the swatches.
- On an empty plate every slot reads as in use, so the dots aren't all faded.
- The colour cells work with the mouse only.
- Slot rows show the dot before the slot number.
- Frame 23b-2's caption needs correcting: "changing the filament keeps the colour" is only true for presets without a default colour.
- Not checked yet:
  - whether each slot gets the right filament list on a printer with two nozzle sizes
  - how the menu itself looks: the harness clicks its rows but photographs only the chip.

Should I commit and open a PR against `jusprin-newui`?

colour and a name -- and seeded one from the open project whenever a
printer with none was selected. Home then showed that seed as "Loaded" on
printers nobody had described, and the setup chat stored the model's
material word where a preset name belonged. The spool concept is gone
(turn 23 of the Prepare wireframes): the chip and its menu now read and
write only what OrcaSlicer already keeps.

- Chip: printer nickname and nozzle (each size when they differ), then
  one dot per project slot -- faded when the current plate does not print
  with it, unused slots folded into "+n" past eight, dots shrunk when more
  than eight are in use -- and the filament's short name when the used
  slots share one, otherwise a count. The rules live in FilamentChipModel,
  which jusprin_tests covers without wx.
- Filament menu: a colour row (the slot's colour, Orca's saved colours,
  "+" for the system picker), the installed filaments that fit in
  brand-then-name order, Other filament... (Orca's own filament page),
  Filament settings... and Add a slot. It stays open, so a filament and a
  colour change in one visit. With several slots a slot list opens first.
  "Use what's loaded on the printer..." leads only when the printer
  reports trays, greyed with the reason while it is offline, and runs
  Orca's own sync unchanged.
- A filament change follows Orca's colour rule (a preset with a default
  colour brings it; otherwise the slot keeps its colour), through one
  per-slot SetupCommands path the Agent's filament change now shares.
- One grey thread line per menu visit that changed a filament, led by the
  colour it landed on; notes gain an optional swatch for that. A
  colour-only visit adds no line.
- Home's Loaded row shows only trays a connected printer reports.
  printer_change saves the nozzle only, and the setup chat is told what is
  loaded only from the printer itself.
- A nozzle change on the project's printer runs the compatibility pass
  Orca's printer switch runs, so a process or filament made for the old
  nozzle is replaced. That is a real change to the project, and the
  harness now expects the project to be modified exactly when something
  was replaced (it was the opposite rule from 7f66e75b07).

The fake Bambu printer can now send a tray's filament id, as hardware
does: Orca's sync skips a tray without one, so without it the sync could
not be exercised.

Verified on Windows: jusprin_tests 52 cases, agent_bridge_tests 258,
jusprin_fake_bambu_tests 10, AgentUI 204 and HomeUI 61 Vitest tests. Shell
harness: --printer-setup 166 checks and --home-live 70 checks pass (the
tray row opens Orca's sync with the sidebar hidden, and the two fake trays
land in the project's slots); the default run passes 433 of 434, the
exception being print_opens_cancellable_native_preflight, which fails the
same way on this machine without these changes.

No OrcaSlicer-owned file is touched.

# Four fixes for the filament chip (branch claude/filament-chip)

All paths are under `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Shell/` unless stated.
Line numbers are at commit a74862697e.

## 1. Colour cells cannot be reached by keyboard

**What is wrong.** In the filament menu, the colour swatches and the "+" cell
respond to the mouse only. A person using the keyboard can change the filament
but not the colour.

**Where.**
- `FilamentMenu.cpp:64` `ColourCell` binds enter, leave and left-button-up, and
  nothing for keys or focus.
- `HeaderControls.cpp:663` `HeaderMenu::on_key` moves only through `m_items`,
  the row buttons. The colour row is built by `set_header_builder`, so it is
  never in that list.

**Expected.**
- Up from the first filament row moves into the colour row. Down leaves it.
- Left and Right move between cells, including "+".
- Return or Space applies the cell, the same as a click.
- The focused cell shows the 2 DIP focus ring the design system requires.
- After a colour is applied the menu rebuilds. The keyboard position stays on
  the same cell.
- Where a keyboard-opened menu starts does not change.

**How to check.** Add harness checks that send keys through the menu's key
handler: reach a saved colour with arrows, press Return, and confirm the slot's
colour changed and the menu stayed open.

## 2. Sizes typed as numbers instead of design tokens

**What is wrong.** The branch adds sizes as typed numbers. The project rule is
in `agent-docs/jusprin/design-system.md`, section "Writing UI code", rules 1
and 2: add the token first, extend the guard, then read it from code.

**Where.** New on this branch:

| Value | Location |
|---|---|
| Slot dot size, 8 and 4 | `HeaderControls.cpp:121-122` |
| Gap between slot dots, 3 and 2 | `HeaderControls.cpp:123-124` |
| Gap from the dots to the label, 8 | `HeaderControls.cpp:263` |
| Fade strength of an unused slot, 90 of 255 | `HeaderControls.cpp:404` |
| Colour cell inset and ring width | `FilamentMenu.cpp:95`, `:102`, `:110` |

Carried over from the old spool menu, still typed: the colour grid gap and
caption gap of 4, at `FilamentMenu.cpp:328` and `:341`.

**Expected.** Each value is a token in
`resources/jusprin/ui/design-tokens.json`, read through `ShellTheme::metrics()`,
with a guard in `tests/brand/test_brand_tokens.cpp`. Follow the existing
`component.swatch` entry: parsed at `ShellTheme.cpp:267`, held in
`SwatchMetrics` in `ShellTheme.hpp:101`.

**Leave alone.** `kFullSizeDots` and `kColoursPerRow` are counts, not sizes.

**How to check.** The guard test fails when a token is removed or changed. The
chip renders the same as before.

## 3. One menu visit can post two chat lines

**What is wrong.** The design posts one grey chat line per menu visit that
changed a filament. A visit ends whenever the popup is dismissed, including
when the menu closes itself to show a dialog and then reopens.

**Where.**
- `FilamentMenu.cpp:144` every popup gets a dismiss listener that calls
  `end_visit`.
- `FilamentMenu.cpp:372` `pick_colour` closes the popup before the system
  colour picker, then reopens it.
- `FilamentMenu.cpp:290` "Other filament…" closes the popup, opens OrcaSlicer's
  filament page, then reopens it.

**Reproduce first.**
1. Open the filament menu and pick a different filament.
2. Click "+", pick a colour, press OK. The menu comes back.
3. Pick another filament.
4. Click away.

I expect two chat lines. I have not run this by hand.

**Expected.** One line, naming the final filament. A visit ends only when the
person leaves the menu: click-away, Esc, Tab, "Filament settings…", or the
sync row. A close that the menu makes itself, followed by a reopen, is the same
visit. If the menu cannot reopen, end the visit so the line is not lost.

**How to check.** The existing checks `the_visit_leaves_one_line` and
`one_menu_visit_posts_one_note` do not cover a close and reopen in the middle.
Add one that does.

## 4. Dot drawn before the slot number

**What is wrong.** In the slot list, each row reads dot, number, name. The
design, frame 23d, reads number, dot, name.

**Where.** `FilamentMenu.cpp:206-207`. The number is part of the label, and the
colour is the row's leading dot, which is drawn before the label at
`HeaderControls.cpp:393`.

**Expected.** Number first, then the dot, then the filament's short name.

**Keep.** The row's name, used for lookup and accessibility, stays
"1  Bambu PLA Basic". The harness check `the_slot_list_names_each_slot`
depends on it.

**How to check.** Render the slot list to a picture in the harness and confirm
the order. The harness currently photographs only the chip.

visit. If the menu cannot reopen, end the visit so the line is not lost.

**How to check.** The existing checks `the_visit_leaves_one_line` and
`one_menu_visit_posts_one_note` do not cover a close and reopen in the middle.
Add one that does.

## 4. Dot drawn before the slot number

**What is wrong.** In the slot list, each row reads dot, number, name. The
design, frame 23d, reads number, dot, name.

**Where.** `FilamentMenu.cpp:206-207`. The number is part of the label, and the
colour is the row's leading dot, which is drawn before the label at
`HeaderControls.cpp:393`.

**Expected.** Number first, then the dot, then the filament's short name.

**Keep.** The row's name, used for lookup and accessibility, stays
"1  Bambu PLA Basic". The harness check `the_slot_list_names_each_slot`
depends on it.

**How to check.** Render the slot list to a picture in the harness and confirm
the order. The harness currently photographs only the chip.

158-Rules for anyone, human or agent, adding or changing a JusPrin surface. They
159-exist because every value that is typed by hand drifts from Figma and from
160-the other side of the app within weeks; today's guards catch most of it, but
161-only if the code goes through the token file in the first place.
162-
163-1. **Never type a color, radius, font, or control size.** Every one comes
164-   from `resources/jusprin/ui/design-tokens.json`. Native code reads it
165-   through `ShellTheme`: `palette(dark)` for color, `metrics()` for radii,
166-   spacing, and per-component sizes, `font(role)` for type. A stock
167-   `wxStaticText`, `wxTextCtrl`, or OrcaSlicer `Button` is
168-   dressed through `Shell/ShellRecipes.hpp`, never by calling its setters
169-   with literals. The Agent page uses only `var(--…)`: `--<group>-<name>` for
170-   color, `--radius-<name>`, `--font-<role>`, `--font-code`, and
171-   `--button-<recipe>-padding`.
172-2. **If the value you need has no token, add the token first.** Put it in
173-   the JSON, extend the guard in `tests/brand/test_brand_tokens.cpp` so a
174-   later edit cannot silently move it, then read it from code. Do not write
175-   the number "for now": the guards cannot see a literal that is already
176-   there, and the next reader cannot tell a decision from an accident. A
177-   value that exists in Figma but not in the roles or scales is a design
178-   decision to raise, not a reason to type it.
179-3. **Layout spacing may stay literal, on the scale.** Padding between
180-   regions, gaps, and margins use 4, 8, 12, 16, 20, 24, 32, 40, or 48 DIP.
181-   Control padding is not layout spacing; it comes from a button recipe.

content.text:
All four fixes are done on `claude/filament-chip`. They're not committed yet.

**1. Colour cells by keyboard.** `HeaderMenu` now accepts a view among its rows that joins its keyboard handling (`HeaderMenuKeyView`), and the colour row is one.
- Up from the first filament row moves into the colour row; Down moves back out.
- Left and Right move between cells, including "+". Return or Space applies a cell, the same as a click.
- The focus ring is 2 DIP, taken from the existing `component.focus.width` token, and drawn in the gap around the cell so the swatch itself doesn't change size.
- The keyboard's place is remembered by colour value, so it stays on the same colour after the rebuild even though the applied colour moves to the front.
- A keyboard-opened menu still starts on the first row.

**2. Tokens.** A new `component.slotDot` table holds the dot sizes, gaps, label gap and fade strength. `component.swatch` gained the cell gap, caption gap, insets, ring widths and the "+" stroke width. `component.focus` is now read by the code too. All three are held in `ShellTheme` metrics and guarded by a new test in `test_brand_tokens.cpp`. I checked the guard by changing one token: the test failed, then passed once the token was restored. The two counts, `kFullSizeDots` and `kColoursPerRow`, are unchanged as you asked.

**3. One line per visit.** The colour picker and "Other filament…" now close the menu as part of the same visit, so that close no longer ends it. Leaving the menu by click-away, Esc, Tab, Filament settings… or the sync row still ends the visit. If the menu can't reopen, the visit ends there so its line isn't lost. I didn't reproduce the double line on the old build first. It follows from the old code, which ended the visit on every close, the picker's included.

**4. Number, dot, name.** Slot rows draw the number ahead of the dot. Rows now carry a separate `name`, so each is still named "1  Bambu PLA Basic" for lookups and screen readers. `name` is the last field in `HeaderMenuItem`, because putting it second broke rows elsewhere that fill the struct positionally.

**Checks run:**
- Keyboard: the harness sends keys through the menu's own key handler. It moves Down, Up, then Right to a saved colour and presses Return. It confirms the slot's colour changed, the menu stayed open, the keyboard stayed on that colour after the rebuild, and Down leaves the row.
- One line across a dialog, on Windows: the harness picks a filament, opens the native picker from "+" and presses OK in it, picks a second filament, then leaves. Exactly one line posts, naming the second filament.
- Slot row picture: the harness renders a slot row to `slot-list-row.png` and reads it left to right. The number is at x=13, the dot at 29, the name from 45.
  - My first version of this check passed for the wrong reason: dark mode's near-white text colour matched the background. It now finds text by contrast against the row's own background.
- Harness runs:
  - Default: 457 of 458 checks pass; the failure is the print-preflight check that fails the same way without these changes.
  - `--home-live`: all 70 checks pass. One earlier run timed out on a Home printing check this work doesn't touch, and it passed on the rerun.
- Other suites: brand tokens and shell theme tests, AgentUI (204) and HomeUI (61) all pass.

Should I commit these and push to `claude/filament-chip`? If you've created the PR by now, that updates it.

cd /c/src/JusPrin; cat > /tmp/msg3.txt <<'EOF'
Replace saved spools with a filament chip built on Orca's own slots

Squash of claude/filament-chip.

The header chip remembered a "spool" per printer -- a filament preset, a
colour and a name -- and seeded one from the open project whenever a
printer with none was selected. Home then showed that seed as "Loaded" on
printers nobody had described, and the setup chat stored the model's
material word where a preset name belonged. The spool concept is gone
(turn 23 of the Prepare wireframes): the chip and its menu now read and
write only what OrcaSlicer already keeps.

- Chip: printer nickname and nozzle (each size when they differ), then one
  dot per project slot -- faded when the current plate does not print with
  it, unused slots folded into "+n" past eight, dots shrunk when more than
  eight are in use -- and the filament's short name when the used slots
  share one, otherwise a count. The rules live in FilamentChipModel, which
  jusprin_tests covers without wx.
- Filament menu: a colour row (the slot's colour, Orca's saved colours, "+"
  for the system picker), the installed filaments that fit in
  brand-then-name order, Other filament... (Orca's own filament page),
  Filament settings... and Add a slot. It stays open, so a filament and a
  colour change in one visit; with several slots a slot list opens first,
  its rows reading number, dot, name. "Use what's loaded on the printer..."
  leads only when the printer reports trays, greyed with the reason while it
  is offline, and runs Orca's own sync unchanged.
- The colour row is reachable by keyboard: HeaderMenu takes a custom view
  into its keyboard model (HeaderMenuKeyView), and the row moves between
  cells, applies one, and draws the 2 DIP focus ring.
- New sizes are tokens (component.slotDot, component.swatch, and the
  existing component.focus), read through ShellTheme and guarded in
  test_brand_tokens.cpp.
- A filament change follows Orca's colour rule (a preset with a default
  colour brings it; otherwise the slot keeps its colour), through one
  per-slot SetupCommands path the Agent's filament change now shares.
- One grey thread line per menu visit that changed a filament, led by the
  colour it landed on; notes gain an optional swatch for that. A close the
  menu makes itself to show a dialog and reopen is the same visit.
- Home's Loaded row shows only trays a connected printer reports.
  printer_change saves the nozzle only, and the setup chat is told what is
  loaded only from the printer itself.
- A nozzle change on the project's printer runs the compatibility pass
  Orca's printer switch runs, so a process or filament made for the old
  nozzle is replaced; the project is then modified exactly when something
  was replaced (the opposite rule from 7f66e75b07).
- The fake Bambu printer can send a tray's filament id, as hardware does;
  Orca's sync skips a tray without one.

Verified on Windows: jusprin_tests, agent_bridge_tests,
jusprin_fake_bambu_tests, brand_tokens_tests and shell_theme_tests pass;
AgentUI 204 and HomeUI 61 Vitest tests pass. Shell harness --printer-setup
166 and --home-live 70 checks pass; the default run passes 457 of 458, the
exception being print_opens_cancellable_native_preflight, which fails the
same way on that machine without this branch.

No OrcaSlicer-owned file is touched.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF
